title: VPN & remote access
blurb: VPN won't connect, remote desktop, working from home.

remedies.title: Everything is slow while the VPN is on
remedies.why: All traffic may go through the office first; distance and busy VPN servers slow it.

steps.text: Connect to the nearest VPN location if the app lets you choose.
Disconnect the VPN when you don't need work-only resources (if policy allows).
Use a cable or better Wi-Fi; VPN adds to any Wi-Fi weakness.

remedies.escalate: IT can check whether Teams and Microsoft 365 bypass the VPN (split tunnel).

remedies.title: VPN keeps disconnecting
remedies.why: Unstable Wi-Fi, sleep, or a session time limit.

steps.text: Fix the Wi-Fi first; VPNs drop with every Wi-Fi hiccup.
Stop the computer sleeping during long transfers.
Stop the computer sleeping during long transfers.

remedies.escalate: Tell IT the times it dropped; sessions may have a time limit.

remedies.title: Getting set up to work from home
remedies.why: A few checks avoid most work-from-home problems.

steps.text: Test the VPN and sign-in before your first day at home.
Use a cable or sit near the router for calls.
A headset with a microphone beats laptop speakers.
Lock the computer when away and keep work files in work storage.

remedies.title: Remote Desktop shows a black screen or is very slow
remedies.why: Display settings, a slow connection or graphics features in the session.

steps.text: Lower the remote session's display quality (Experience tab: choose a slower connection).
Use one monitor in the session instead of all.
Press Ctrl+Alt+End then cancel to refresh a black session (Windows client).
